page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a memory-optimized and storage-focused virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 2880 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations (6.17 million operations per second) fall within the average range. However, memory read bandwidth is relatively weak, with small-block cached reads at 303.46 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 36.73 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth is average at 27.93 GB/sec.

The server's hardware profile offers high resource density, combining a large 2880 GB local NVMe SSD with a generous memory allocation, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring fast local scratch space and moderate memory capacity. However, the weak memory read bandwidth and lower multi-threaded decompression speeds present a tradeoff for memory-bound parallel processing. This instance is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, text processing, and light LLM inference tasks using small models.
